lead.question:
∀ (q : Fin 3 → ℝ) (a : Fin 3 → (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))),
    AffineIndependent ℝ a → (∀ i, q i ≠ 0) →
    (∀ x ∈ equilibria q a, HasNondegenerateHessianAt (potential q a) x) →
    {x : (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) | x ∈ affineSpan ℝ (Set.range a) ∧ x ∉ Set.range a ∧
      (∑ i, (-q i / ‖x - a i‖ ^ 3) • (x - a i)) = 0}.encard ≤ 4

/-- The count when the three distinct sites are collinear. -/
lead.title: The Maxwell conjecture — three charges · step 1

review.statement: For every q : Fin 3 → ℝ and every a : Fin 3 → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3), assume AffineIndependent ℝ a, assume q i ≠ 0 for every i, and assume HasNondegenerateHessianAt (potential q a) x for every x ∈ equilibria q a. Then the set of x in affineSpan ℝ (Set.range a), outside Set.range a, satisfying ∑ i, (−q i / ‖x − a i‖³) • (x − a i) = 0 has encard at most 4. Affine independence makes this the noncollinear case. The collinear comment in the supplied excerpt concerns a different case.
review.significance: The original paper by Philip Arathoon, Gavin Ball, and Matthew D. Kvalheim refutes the general Maxwell bound using five charges and records a three-charge configuration attaining four. Shiva Kintali’s later manuscript proves the matching upper bound for arbitrary nonzero signed strengths when the critical set is finite. [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27197v1) · [Kintali’s Theorem 1](https://shivakintali.github.io/papers/Maxwell3.pdf)
review.settlement_test: A proof must cover every signed nonzero charge triple and every affinely independent site triple under the global Hessian hypothesis. A counterexample must exhibit five distinct counted equilibria in one such configuration and verify the Hessian hypothesis at every equilibrium. Formal completion requires an independent kernel replay against the exact upstream declaration.
review.aliases: Three-charge Maxwell bound, three-point-charge case of Maxwell’s conjecture, and the Coulomb equilibrium bound for three charges. Ya-Lun Tsai proved the equal-magnitude case in 2015. Gabrielov, Dmitry Novikov, and Shapiro obtained the earlier bound of 12. Gabrielov, Dmitry Novikov, T. Novikov, and Shapiro later obtained 6 for positive charges. Kintali’s A Sharp Maxwell Bound for Three Point Charges covers this target. [Tsai](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167278915001347) · [Bound of 12](https://www.wisdom.weizmann.ac.il/~dnovikov/Papers/MaxwellPublished.pdf) · [Bound of 6](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28785) · [Bound of 4](https://shivakintali.github.io/papers/Maxwell3.pdf)

review.proof_or_witness: Informal proof using Shiva Kintali’s Theorem 1. Away from the sites, the displayed vector field is the gradient of V(x) = ∑ᵢ qᵢ/‖x−aᵢ‖. At a zero, put cᵢ = qᵢ/‖x−aᵢ‖³ and S = ∑ᵢ cᵢ. Then Sx = ∑ᵢ cᵢaᵢ. If S = 0, affine independence forces all cᵢ = 0, a contradiction. Thus every zero lies in the affine plane and has barycentric coordinates λᵢ = cᵢ/S. The zero set is semialgebraic. Introduce positive radii rᵢ satisfying rᵢ² = ‖x−aᵢ‖², clear the positive denominator ∏ᵢ rᵢ³, and project onto x. The Hessian hypothesis and inverse function theorem make every zero isolated. A discrete semialgebraic set is finite by cell decomposition. Affine independence also makes the sites distinct, so Kintali’s finite-critical-set theorem gives at most four, which is the required encard bound. [Kintali’s theorem](https://shivakintali.github.io/papers/Maxwell3.pdf)
review.remaining_obligation: For a direct Lean proof using the nondegeneracy hypothesis, the main remaining lemma is that for every noncollinear site triple and every q with all entries nonzero, at most one nonsite point in the site plane satisfies both [λᵢ(x)‖x−aᵢ‖³] = [qᵢ] in real projective space and det(D²(V restricted to the site plane)(x)) > 0. This is the part of Kintali’s Proposition 9.1 needed here. Formalize it and the planar degree identity N = 2m + 3 − w∞, where m counts positive determinants and w∞ is 1 for nonzero total charge and 2 for zero total charge. The ambient Hessian has normal eigenvalue −S, so ambient nondegeneracy gives an invertible planar Hessian. An independent checker still needs the upstream file, a complete Lean proof of these steps or of the stronger cited theorem, and a kernel replay. [Kintali, Section 9](https://shivakintali.github.io/papers/Maxwell3.pdf)
